strategies.name: Sequential All-Reduce with Local Coupling
strategies.desc: Implements the algorithm as-is with 8 sequential all-reduce dispatches, each preceded by local bidiagonal coupling and followed by local uncoupling operations. 8 collective dispatches total. Represents the straightforward translation with no optimization—highest dispatch count but simplest control flow.

strategies.name: Fused Coupling in Overlapped Buffers
strategies.desc: Merges the "undo previous coupling" and "apply next coupling" operations into a single fused local computation between all-reduces, reducing redundant passes over the W×S tensor. Still 8 all-reduce dispatches but halves local memory bandwidth by eliminating intermediate buffers. Trades code complexity for memory efficiency.

strategies.name: Reduce-Scatter then All-Gather Pattern
strategies.desc: Replace each all-reduce with a reduce-scatter (each rank holds one shard) followed by ring-based neighbor exchanges for bidiagonal terms, then all-gather to reconstruct full vector. 8×2=16 collective dispatches but each operates on 1/W payload size. Optimizes for bandwidth-limited networks where smaller messages win despite more rounds.

strategies.name: Hierarchical Two-Level Reduction Tree
strategies.desc: Exploits 224=32×7 factorization (or other) to perform intra-node all-reduces (smaller world size) then inter-node all-reduces, applying coupling at appropriate granularity. Approximately 8×2=16 dispatches but with asymmetric costs. Optimizes for multi-node topology where local collectives are much cheaper than cross-node.

strategies.name: Pipelined Allreduce with Chunked Data
strategies.desc:
Partition the W×S tensor into multiple chunks and pipeline the 8-stage process across chunks, launching the next chunk's stage-k all-reduce while computing stage-(k+1) coupling for the previous chunk. Maintains 8 logical stages but overlaps communication and computation through asynchronous dispatch. Hides local computation latency behind network transfers.
